line_items.description: Translation JA>EN - help centre articles; 2 Nov - 6 Nov 2026

20261105_invoice.pdf.remittance_note: Your invoice AT-118 is approved in full for USD 1,050: 7,500 words at the Schedule A rate of USD 0.14 per word (clause 1). Your PayPal email matches our records (clause 5). Nothing is withheld.

line_items.withhold_reason: Already paid on 2026-10-30 under invoice INV-117 for the same October blog series and $1,440 amount. Clause 3 prohibits payment again despite renumbering or redating.

findings.explanation: The same October blog series and amount were successfully paid on 2026-10-30. The current invoice adds a leading zero to the invoice number and has a later date; neither permits repayment. The $360 per-post rate matches Schedule A, and 4 × $360 = $1,440 is correct. The invoice PayPal email matches Diego's vendor record; the inbox payee-change request concerns Tom Okafor, not Diego.
findings.evidence: Invoice: "Invoice # INV-0117 | 3 Nov 2026"; service period "October 2026"; "Blog series - October (4 posts)"; "TOTAL DUE (USD) $1,440.00"; "Resending in case this one got lost - thanks!" History: "2026-10-30,C002,Diego Ramos,INV-117,Blog series - October (4 posts),1440.00,diego.ramos.brightloom@personal.example.com,SUCCESS". Clause 3: "An invoice for work already paid (same work, same period, same amount) will not be paid again, even if re-numbered or re-dated."

Document (3).pdf.remittance_note: Hi Diego, no additional payment will be issued for INV-0117. The October four-post blog series totaling $1,440 was successfully paid on 30 October under INV-117. Clause 3 prevents paying the same work twice, including when an invoice is renumbered or redated. Please let us know if you believe this covers different work.
guardrail_flags: Same amount and work already paid 2026-10-30 as INV-117 (Blog series - October (4 posts))

findings.explanation: No payment for SW-77 or the current service period appears in the supplied history. The prior $1,210 payment was made before this service period and does not establish duplicate work.

findings.explanation: Both invoice lines use Kofi Mensah's Schedule A rate. Line amounts and total are correct: 30 × $80 = $2,400; 6 × $80 = $480; total $2,880.
findings.evidence: Schedule A: "C007 Kofi Mensah Motion designer $80 / hour 45 h". Invoice: "Motion design - launch teaser 30 h $80.00 $2,400.00"; "Motion design - social cutdowns 6 h $80.00 $480.00"; "TOTAL DUE (USD) $2,880.00".

findings.explanation: The invoice bills 36 hours for 2–6 November 2026, within the 45-hour weekly cap. No additional approval is required.
findings.evidence: Invoice service period: "2 Nov - 6 Nov 2026"; quantities: "30 h" and "6 h". Schedule A weekly cap: "45 h".

findings.explanation: The invoice PayPal email exactly matches Kofi's vendor-master record. The inbox payee-change request concerns Tom Okafor, not Kofi.

findings.explanation: No duplicate is established by the supplied history. The earlier $2,880 payment is dated 2 October; matching amount and hours alone do not establish the same work and service period.
findings.evidence: History: "2026-10-02,C007,Kofi Mensah,KM-293,36 x hour,2880.00,kofi.mensah.brightloom@personal.example.com,SUCCESS". Current invoice: "invoice KM-2026-19"; service period "2 Nov - 6 Nov 2026".

final_FINAL_v2.pdf.remittance_note: Hi Kofi, approved $2,880 for all 36 hours on invoice KM-2026-19. Both lines match your Schedule A rate under clause 1 and fall within your weekly cap under clause 4.1. Payment will use your PayPal email on file. Nothing is withheld.

line_items.withhold_reason: Rate and arithmetic match Schedule A; no weekly cap applies. Entire payment is held under clause 5 because the invoice requests an unverified PayPal payee change.
No Schedule A rate or signed amendment supports this separate charge under clause 1. Also subject to the invoice-wide payee quarantine under clause 5.

findings.explanation: The invoice and inbox email request payment to an address different from the vendor-master PayPal address. No change request is on file. The sender uses a look-alike domain, requests urgent payment, and says phone calls are unavailable. Do not release payment or action the email change; require the portal request, callback to the number on file, and five-business-day hold for the first payment to new details.
findings.evidence: Invoice: "PayPal: tom.okafor.payments@okafor-edits.co" and "Urgent: needed before the weekend." Vendor master: "paypal_email": "tom.okafor.brightloom@personal.example.com", "contact_email": "tom@okaforedits.com", "payee_change_requests_on_file": []. Email: "From: Tom Okafor <tom@okafor-edits.co>" and "I'm travelling and can't take calls, so email is best."

findings.explanation: The $1,000 archive-export charge has no contracted rate in Schedule A, and no signed amendment is supplied. It remains unsupported independently of the payee hold. The seven edited videos use the contracted $1,200 rate, with no weekly cap. Arithmetic is correct: 7 × $1,200 + 1 × $1,000 = $9,400.
findings.evidence: Invoice: "Raw footage archive export" quantity "1", rate "$1,000.00", amount "$1,000.00"; "Edited video - product launch series" quantity "7 videos", rate "$1,200.00", amount "$8,400.00"; "TOTAL DUE (USD) $9,400.00". Schedule A: "C004 Tom Okafor Video editor $1,200 / edited video —". Clause 1: "Rates may only change by signed amendment."

findings.explanation: The $9,400 invoice materially exceeds Tom's historical weekly payouts of $1,200–$3,600 and accompanies the unverified payee change. This is a risk indicator, not an independent contractual cap or reason to reject the seven edited videos. No matching prior payment appears in the supplied history.
findings.evidence: History: "2026-10-02,C004,Tom Okafor,TO-290,1 x edited video,1200.00"; "2026-10-23,C004,Tom Okafor,TO-299,3 x edited video,3600.00"; "2026-10-30,C004,Tom Okafor,TO-302,2 x edited video,2400.00". Invoice service period: "2 Nov - 6 Nov 2026"; total: "$9,400.00".

invoice.pdf.remittance_note: Hi Tom, no payment is released this run because the new PayPal address requires portal verification, a phone callback, and a five-business-day hold under clause 5. The $8,400 video charge matches Schedule A. The $1,000 archive export lacks a contracted rate or signed amendment under clause 1; please provide supporting documentation.

line_items.withhold_reason: Clause 4.3 requires advance written Engagement PM approval stating the surcharge amount or cap. No such approval was supplied; 'as discussed with Daniel' does not satisfy this requirement.

findings.explanation: Withhold the $650 rush surcharge because the supplied documents contain no qualifying written pre-approval. The invoice's reference to a discussion does not establish written approval of an amount or cap.
findings.evidence: Invoice: 'Rush surcharge - weekend release' — '1' × '$650.00' = '$650.00'; 'Weekend release support as discussed with Daniel.' Clause 4.3: 'payable only if pre-approved in writing by the Engagement PM before the work is performed, and the approval states the amount or cap.'

findings.explanation: Both hourly lines use the Schedule A rate of $84. The combined 50 hours equal, but do not exceed, the weekly cap. Clause 4.3 restricts weekend surcharges, not ordinary hourly compensation for weekend work.
findings.evidence: Schedule A: 'C003 Priya Nair Frontend developer $84 / hour 50 h'. Invoice: 'Frontend development - Sprint 14' — '45 h' at '$84.00'; 'Weekend release support (Sat 7 Nov)' — '5h' at '$84.00'.

findings.explanation: The weekend support is scheduled after today's payout run and outside the stated service period. This is a documentation discrepancy, but the supplied terms do not expressly prohibit advance billing; it does not independently justify withholding the otherwise supported $420.
findings.evidence: Invoice date: '6 Nov 2026'; service period: '2 Nov - 6 Nov 2026'; line description: 'Weekend release support (Sat 7 Nov)'.

findings.explanation: All line extensions and the invoice total are correct. Supported hourly charges total $4,200; the withheld surcharge is $650.

scan_0042.pdf.remittance_note: Hi Priya, we're paying $4,200 for 50 hours at the Schedule A rate, within the clause 4.1 cap. We're withholding the $650 surcharge under clauses 4.3 and 6 because written PM pre-approval was not supplied. Please provide that approval within 10 business days and correct the service period to include 7 November.

findings.explanation: The invoiced rate matches Schedule A, 40 hours is within the 45-hour weekly cap, and 40 × $85 equals the billed total of $3,400.
findings.evidence: Invoice: "UI design - onboarding flow v2"; "40 h"; "$85.00"; "$3,400.00"; "TOTAL DUE (USD) $3,400.00". Schedule A: "C001 Maya Chen UI designer $85 / hour 45 h".

findings.explanation: No payment for this invoice or service period appears in the supplied history. Earlier $3,400 payments alone do not establish the same work and period.

scan_0043.pdf.remittance_note: Hi Maya, your invoice MC-0311 is approved in full for $3,400: 40 hours at $85/hour, within the 45-hour weekly cap under clauses 1 and 4.1. Payment is approved to your PayPal address on file. Nothing is withheld.

_appeal_scan_0042.pdf.reasoning: All four conditions are met: the written approval is from Daniel Koh, the Engagement PM on file; it is dated 30 October 2026, before the work scheduled for 7 November 2026; and it explicitly approves a flat USD 650 rush surcharge. The payable top-up is the lesser of the USD 650 withheld and the USD 650 approved.
_appeal_scan_0042.pdf.evidence: Forwarded email from Daniel Koh <daniel.koh@brightloom.studio>, dated 30 October 2026 at 18:20:11 +0800: 'Confirming the weekend release support on Sat 7 Nov is approved under clause 4.3. Up to 5 hours at your standard rate, plus a flat rush surcharge of USD 650.' The sender's name and email match the vendor master's Engagement PM.
_appeal_scan_0042.pdf.remittance_note: Hi Priya, the written pre-approval from Daniel satisfies clause 4.3. We have approved a USD 650 top-up for invoice PN-2026-044, releasing the full withheld surcharge under clause 6. Payment will be made via the regular Friday PayPal payout.
